Passed the fake-backend gate with no warning: G1-G9 all pass, failed [] (report_digest sha256:0d304d6ed284bd7e6a73a17653647bb7a3193811e11b70175eecade5818ff8c5). Evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored and unreviewed: reviewed_by is null, nothing ran on a ScanImage server or a microscope, and no hardware run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is PythonObjectDriver, but its writes binding calls a native with the single value (mhs/bridge/python.py _compile_writes sets positional ['value']), while the upstream setter is si_set(serv_var, value) with a constant service-variable name. A direct Driver over the same confirmed entry symbol (py_json_client:ScanimageTcpipClient, py_json_client.py:19) expresses si_get/si_set without changing the protocol; native.py opens the upstream client for the hardware view. The card's decision is direct-driver, so no decision change is implied.

MOCK PATH: the card prefers upstream-sim. The clone's stand-in is dummy_json_server.py, a TCP server that waits for a socket connection (dummy_json_server.py:97-105); the gate runs without network, so the package ships an in-package recording fake of the client object (fake.py) with the same public methods and reply shapes as the upstream client and its dummy server. Starting the upstream server would also require importing and running clone code, which this task forbids.

BOUND CAPABILITY SET: one read and one write of the ScanImage property hSI.hRoiManager.scanZoomFactor (JsonClientTest.m:12-19, test_matlab_jsonserver.py:30-31), plus the clone's hSI.startFocus feval example. The write has an operator_required limit because the clone states no allowed range (the example set value 10 is not a bound); site-limits.example.json is only a template and every write is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site supplies its range. Risk R1 reflects this bound set (a configuration write and a focus call); the loader's reviewed_by refusal applies only at R2/R3, so it is not claimed here.

NOT COVERED: (1) arbitrary si_eval and si_feval, which execute Matlab on the ScanImage host; only the clone's fixed hSI.startFocus example is bound, because a free-form expression input cannot be bounded or reviewed. (2) Generic si_get/si_set of other server properties, including the photostimulation and imaging power the README says the client is used for (README.md:3): the clone gives no property name, type or range for power, and a generic string property input would be an unbounded path to the laser; a site that binds power control must raise the risk and supply the bounds. (3) Image data and imaging-series control: the client protocol carries only JSON values and eval/feval outputs, no image array, so cap.imaging.capture.v1 is not exposed. (4) The upstream test scripts' direct network examples are not replayed; the fake records calls in memory instead.

SAFETY: the native stop is close() (py_json_client.py:35-36), the only teardown the client offers; the e-stop closes the control socket, after which the runtime latches and refuses all further writes and actions. This is not an independent hardware stop and no estop_physical_ref is claimed; an acquisition already running on the ScanImage host is not stopped by closing the socket, so the deployed microscope must keep its own physical stop within reach. The safe_state sentence says exactly that. The fake's close is observable and is reached by the e-stop and by teardown.

check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-30; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after reviewer edits: the action x-cap.histedlab.start_focus.v1 was removed. hSI.startFocus starts a focus acquisition, in which a two-photon microscope scans its laser over the sample, and close(), the e-stop, does not stop it (the author's safe_state said so); no line of the clone names a ScanImage stop, so a driver that starts it could not stop it. The package keeps the zoom read and the operator_required zoom write at R1. driver.py, test_driver.py, the reference and the catalogue request of RESULT.json changed.
